content.text: {"answer":"Yes—several supplied papers report geometry-aware or geometry-motivated optimizers beating Adam on non-convex or curved loss landscapes, though not all papers agree that geometry itself is the reason. ArcGD, a geometrically motivated optimizer, was evaluated on a stochastic non-convex Rosenbrock function and on CIFAR-10 MLPs; it consistently outperformed Adam in one Rosenbrock setting and usually reached better final solutions in another, while also achieving higher average test accuracy than Adam on CIFAR-10 [1]. Muon also consistently improved over Adam on ModelNet40 across several equivariant and geometric architectures, with analyses suggesting more regular loss surfaces despite larger Hessian curvature summaries [2]. EISAM likewise outperformed Adam across benchmark datasets and architectures, with theory tying this to flatter minima and reduced curvature [6].\n\nThat said, one paper argues against a simple “geometry wins” story: Muon-like gains may come more from local alignment and descent potential than from any precise global geometry, and even a deliberately structure-free optimizer can match Muon [5]. Another paper supports Muon over Adam from a curvature view, finding Muon gets a larger one-step loss decrease because it pays a smaller second-order curvature penalty and has lower normalized directional sharpness [8].","grounded":true}
